title: Angular Build System Fundamentals knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Angular Build System Fundamentals”?
options: Angular Build System Fundamentals should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Angular Build System Fundamentals helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Angular Build System Fundamentals means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Angular Build System Fundamentals removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Angular Build System Fundamentals helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Angular Build System Fundamentals is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Angular CLI build” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Angular CLI build” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Angular CLI build” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Angular CLI build” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Angular CLI build” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Angular CLI build” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Angular CLI build” under Angular Build System Fundamentals. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Angular Build System Fundamentals”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
